back: Movement of assimilates (e.g. sucrose, amino acids) in the phloem from sources to sinks, using energy.
Source: releases assimilates into phloem (e.g. a leaf). Sink: removes them for use or storage (e.g. root, fruit, growing bud).
Proton pumps (ATP) move H⁺ out; H⁺ returns via sucrose-proton cotransporters, bringing sucrose in; sucrose passes to sieve tube via plasmodesmata.
Loading lowers ψ → water enters by osmosis → high pressure at source; unloading at sink lowers pressure → sap flows down the pressure gradient.
Sap flows from a cut stylet: phloem sap is under positive pressure.
Removing a ring of bark (phloem) makes sugars accumulate above the ring: assimilates move in phloem.
Soluble, non-reducing (unreactive), carries more energy per molecule.
Xylem: tension from transpiration (passive). Phloem: hydrostatic pressure from active loading.
Different solutes at different speeds; flow in opposite directions; sieve plates resist flow.
